description:
Prove, with a counting stand-in configured as the git executable, that `query available` and `issue show` start at most one git process in a primary checkout and in a linked checkout.

## Background

- Layout detection is one probe process per invocation, and issue reads use the checkout's own data root plus, in a linked checkout, the primary checkout's data root, with no git process.
- `jit::test_harness` provides a counting stand-in: a `git` file in its own directory that records each invocation and runs the real git. Prepending that directory to the spawned `jit` process's `PATH` configures it as the git executable for that child only, so no process-wide state changes.
- Before the probe collapsed to one process, both commands started three `git rev-parse` processes in a primary checkout; in a linked checkout they also started one `git show` per issue missing locally.
- The `cli_repo_workflow` suite gathers its tests as modules listed in `crates/jit/tests/cli_repo_workflow/main.rs`, so a new module adds no test target (`@/inv/bounded-rust-build-footprint`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A `cli_repo_workflow` module runs `jit query available --json` and `jit issue show <id> --json` in a primary checkout with the stand-in first on `PATH`, and asserts that each records at most one git invocation.
- [hard] REQ-02: The module runs both commands in a linked checkout for an issue that only the primary checkout's data root holds, and asserts that each reads the issue and records at most one git invocation.
- [hard] REQ-03: A failing assertion prints the recorded invocations.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.
title: CLI test bounds the git processes of issue reads
